pages.text: A permanent magnet is set by a field stronger than its $(thing)coercivity$(), and keeps what it was given. Ferrite needs about 0.35 T, neodymium-iron-boron 1.2 T, samarium-cobalt 2 T.

The rare earths come from $(item)Monazite Sand$(), which the Spectrograph picks out of ordinary sand and separates into $(item)Rare Earth Oxide$(). Monazite carries a little thorium: it is weakly radioactive.
The $(item)Magnetizer$() gives 0.6 T from its coil alone. An iron core multiplies a coil's field: each block of iron (or any block tagged $(thing)magnetic$()) touching the Magnetizer adds 0.35 T.
